    {"name":"--fit-thresholds","type":"flag","default":"false","description":"#1024: after the LM iterations, fit by an exact 1-D search every constant that is an operand of a comparison (greater, less, greater_or_equal, less_or_equal, equal) or sits in the condition of if (directly or as the constant of a sub or add against a constant), which the LM never moves because its adjoint is zero. The candidates are the midpoints between consecutive sorted operand values on the fit rows, scored in levels of at most 64 that narrow around the best until every midpoint of the range is scored (at most 192 evaluations per threshold for 65,535 midpoints); the loss is the one the constants are fitted on (weighted squared error for the squared family and for --fitness pnl, the configured metric otherwise); the start value is kept unless a candidate is strictly better; ties keep the start, then the smaller absolute threshold. At most 2 constants per tree; constants under an aggregate, a custom block or a meta operator are never fitted. After a move the other constants are refit once on the new partition. Applies to the search fit, the prune refit and the exact finalist refit. A tree with such a constant takes the exact CPU fit arm, never the device, so the ledger counts it under the fallback cause threshold_constant. No effect with --fit-iters 0. Reported as threshold_moves in the development log (fit). A saved search setting: a resume refuses a different value; a checkpoint without it loads as off"},

    {"name":"--reject-fixed-position","type":"flag","default":"false","description":"#848: under --fitness pnl, reject offspring and random fill or restart trees whose long/flat position cannot depend on the inputs before the constant fit, and keep them out of the archive and the rebuilt front. Before the constant fit the test takes every constant as the whole real line, so only a tree no constant values could make selective is rejected; archive admission and the rebuilt front test the fitted values. The test is the exact output range of the tree over all real inputs: a range that does not cross --threshold (a boundary that touches it counts) fixes the position, for example gauss(c * x), exp(c * x) and logistic(c * x) at threshold 0 (the same trees cross a threshold of 1e-30). Such a tree prices buy and hold or takes flat rows from float underflow, never a signal; the device f32 program underflows earlier than f64, so the two backends can rank it differently. Operators without a range rule count as unbounded, so the test only rejects what it proves. Counted in the development log as variation.fixed_position_rejected. Seeds and migrants are never filtered. When every candidate is fixed the front keeps them and the run JSON search.fixed_position_front_fallback is true. The search effect needs --fitness pnl and input variables. With --objective (#849) the flag also makes a member with a fixed position unusable as finalist under any --fitness: its objective is null and objective.usable_candidates counts it out (so does a validation book that was long on every row or on none, whatever the threshold: fixed_position_realised); run.json reports validation_book.fixed_position (long, flat or null) for every member and objective.finalist.fixed_position without the flag.     {"name":"--restart-policy","type":"enum","default":"archive","description":"#1022: archive | island. Which stall rule restarts an island at every restart interval (60 generations). archive: an island restarts after two checks in which its best error is worse than the archive best; once ring migration has spread the archive best to every island no island is ever behind it, so no restart fires. island: an island restarts when its own best error has not improved (relative 1e-9, the patience rule) for one restart interval, except the keeper, the lowest island whose best error equals the archive best; the restarted island takes no front parent and no migrant for --restart-isolation generations. With --islands 1 the only island is the keeper and nothing restarts. Applies to the node path and the flat postfix path. An isolated island also takes no --qd-policy parent (neither its global-front share nor a QD-archive parent): it breeds from its own members only (#1067). Saved search setting: a resume refuses a different value; a checkpoint without it loads as archive; island adds island_stall records to the checkpoint. The development log carries restarts, restarts_total and isolated"},
